request: find general contractors and construction firms that might want robotics for materials handling, mid-size, US

queries: general contractor "prefabrication facility" opens new shop 2024 2025 press release construction
"top 400 contractors" ENR regional midwest general contractor prefab shop equipment yard
mid-size general contractor "VDC" OR "virtual design and construction" "innovation" team construction technology adoption site:*.com
construction company hiring "yard manager" OR "logistics coordinator" OR "warehouse supervisor" jobs general contractor
general contractor "distribution center" OR "warehouse construction" specialist builder portfolio projects United States
"multi-trade prefabrication" OR "offsite construction" general contractor invests expansion new facility square feet
industrial contractor "laydown yard" OR "material staging" large project announcement data center warehouse build
construction firm pilot robotics OR automation jobsite "we partnered" press release general contractor innovation lab

rubric.criterion: US-based general contractor or construction firm with roughly $50M-$1B annual revenue (regional/mid-market, not a national top-20 ENR giant or a small local builder)
rubric.why: ICP specifies mid-size US GCs; this size band has budget for a pilot but short enough decision chains to move fast.

rubric.criterion: Operates its own physical materials footprint: a warehouse, equipment/laydown yard, prefab or modular shop, or tool crib under their direct control
rubric.why: The robots move pallets and carts; the prospect must own a controlled indoor/yard space where a pilot can be deployed without a client's permission.

rubric.criterion: Evidence of repetitive manual material hauling at volume - e.g. multi-trade prefab assembly lines, kitting operations, large yard staging for industrial jobs
rubric.why: Directly maps to the pain the robot removes (crew hours spent hauling), making the ROI story concrete rather than hypothetical.

rubric.criterion: Visible innovation capacity: a VDC/BIM team, director of innovation or construction technology, lean construction program, or prior tech pilots (drones, layout robots, wearables)
rubric.why: Signals an internal champion and an existing process for evaluating and funding pilots - the main predictor of a 15-min call converting.

rubric.criterion: Recent growth or investment signal in the last 18 months: new prefab facility, yard/warehouse expansion, relocation to a larger campus, or hiring for logistics/warehouse/equipment roles
rubric.why: Capex and hiring around materials handling is the moment when automation gets considered as an alternative to adding headcount or square footage.

rubric.criterion: Project mix weighted toward large industrial, warehouse, distribution-center, data center or manufacturing builds
rubric.why: These project types have big laydown yards and heavy palletized material flow, and the GC often becomes a reference into the owner's own warehouse operations.

disqualifiers: Residential homebuilders, small remodelers, or specialty trade subs under ~$50M revenue - no owned yard or prefab shop and no budget for a pilot
Top-tier ENR national contractors (Turner, Bechtel, Kiewit-scale) - procurement cycles and incumbent vendor relationships are too slow for an early pilot
Pure design firms, architects, engineering consultancies, developers, or owner's reps - they never physically handle materials
Asset-light GCs that subcontract 100% of self-perform work and lease jobsite-only space with no permanent warehouse or yard
Non-US firms or US firms whose operations are entirely overseas - support, safety and compliance footprint doesn't match
Companies already running a competing AMR/jobsite robotics deployment at scale, or that sell construction robotics themselves (competitor, not prospect)
Firms in visible financial distress, bankruptcy, or recently acquired and mid-integration - no discretionary pilot spend

companies.name: C.D. Smith Construction
companies.location: Fond du Lac, WI (offices in Milwaukee, Madison, La Crosse)

facts.fact: Self-performs concrete, masonry, precast and steel erection, earthwork, heavy equipment operation, and millwright + equipment moving services
Completed a 21,350 sq ft paint line warehouse addition for Pierce Manufacturing in Appleton, WI in six months
Norbert 'Norb' Schmidt joined as President, reporting to CEO Justin Smith

companies.fit_reason: Mid-size WI GC that self-performs heavy equipment work and equipment moving and builds warehouses for manufacturers; new President with an operational-excellence background.

final.subject: moving material for your self-perform crews
final.body:
Hi Norb,

I was reading C.D. Smith's industrial page and noticed how much you self-perform, from steel erection and precast to heavy equipment operation and equipment moving.

We build autonomous mobile robots that move pallets, carts and materials around warehouses and logistics yards, and they're already deployed in supply-chain and warehouse operations. We're now looking at construction, where crews spend a lot of hours hauling materials around yards, prefab shops and job sites.

Would you be open to a 15-minute intro call to see if a small pilot in your yard or prefab shop makes sense?

Alex
